title: Platform Systems & Services: Playbook, Dashboards, Runbooks, Retro, and Roadmap (Q1 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Canonical Q1 2026 playbook for Platform Systems & Services covering service ownership, operational dashboards, alerting thresholds, runbooks for critical failure modes, key retrospective findings from Q4 2025 incidents, and the roadmap for next-phase reliability and automation work.
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates operational guidance for the Platform Systems & Services team: core services, ownership, how-to procedures (deploys, incident triage), dashboards and alerts (recommended panels and alert thresholds), runbooks for critical failure modes, Q4 2025 retrospectives and resulting action items, and a prioritized roadmap for Q2-Q3 2026. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, SREs, and engineering managers.

Scope:
- Systems covered: platform-controller, metrics-ingest, alert-processor, dashboards-api, platform-proxy, ci-cd-orchestrator, secrets-sync.
- Excluded: model-serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime docs), customer-facing API product pages.

Key contacts and ownership:
- Platform Controller: owner=platform-controller-service (team: infra-platform), primary on-call: @diego (PagerDuty schedule: platform-controller).
- Metrics Ingest: owner=observability-team, primary on-call: @samantha.
- Alert Processor: owner=platform-ops, primary on-call: @rajiv.
- Dashboards API & UI: owner=eng-platform, primary on-call: rotation across oncall-ui.
- CI/CD Orchestrator: owner=eng-infra, primary on-call: infra-oncall.

SLOs and Error Budget policy (service-level):
- Platform Controller: availability SLO 99.95% monthly; latency P95 < 120ms for control-plane RPCs. Error budget burn triggers an SLO review in Slack #platform-slo.
- Metrics Ingest: data completeness 99.9% per 24h window; pipeline lag < 90s.
- Dashboards API: availability 99.9%; chart render TTFB P95 < 300ms.

Dashboards (recommended panels and owners):
- Platform Overview (dash-id: platform-overview-main):
  - Active nodes / capacity by region (owner: infra-platform)
  - API success rate, 5m & 1h windows (owner: eng-platform)
  - Control-plane latency heatmap (owner: platform-controller)
  - KV cache hit rate (owner: serving-runtime)

- Observability Pipeline (dash-id: obs-pipeline):
  - Ingest throughput (events/s), backlog in processing queue (seconds), consumer lags (owner: observability).
  - Alert counts by severity + alert processor error rates.

- CI/CD Orchestrator (dash-id: cicd-orch):
  - Active runs, median run time, failure rate per repo (owner: eng-infra).

Alerting rules and thresholds (examples):
- platform-controller_high_error_rate (SEV=high): trigger when API 5m error rate > 2% AND sustained for 3 minutes. PagerDuty: P1. Escalation: primary on-call -> secondary -> eng-LEAD.
- metrics-ingest_backlog (SEV=high): trigger when processing backlog > 10 minutes for > 5 minutes. PagerDuty: P1.
- dashboards_render_error (SEV=medium): > 1% render error rate for 10m. Slack alert to #platform-alerts, no immediate PD unless user impact confirmed.
- disk_pressure_node (SEV=high): node disk usage > 90% for > 2 minutes. Automations: cordon + notify infra-oncall.

Runbooks (top-level procedures) - copy these into the service-specific runbooks stored under /runbooks in the team wiki:  

1) Runbook: platform-controller: control-plane 5xx spike
- Symptoms: sudden spike in 5xxs across control-plane APIs; P95 latency increases > 2x baseline.
- Immediate checks (first 10 minutes):
  1. Check platform-overview: CPU/GPU control-plane nodes by region and recent scaling events.
  2. Query logs: `kubectl -n platform logs -l app=platform-controller --since=15m` and scan for repeated errors / OOMs.
  3. Look at metrics-ingest backlog and alert-processor errors - correlated backlog often causes downstream 5xxs.
- Mitigations (ordered):
  1. If CPU or memory exhausted on some pods: scale replica count by factor 2 (temporary) and set annotation `redwood.platform/incident-override=true`.
  2. If a particular release shows high errors: rollback to last stable tag (documented in release notes) using the CI/CD rollback playbook.
  3. If disk pressure on control-plane nodes detected: drain affected node, provision replacement, and restore from artifacts.
- Post-incident actions: attach logs + traces to incident ticket, run SLO burn analysis, and open a follow-up Jira ticket for root cause fix.

2) Runbook: metrics-ingest: consumer lag high
- Symptoms: consumer lag > 300s, metrics pipeline backlog grows.
- Immediate checks:
  1. Inspect consumer group offsets in Kafka (or Kinesis): `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group metrics-ingest` or Kinesis monitoring panel.
  2. Check alert-processor and downstream storage (Cassandra/ClickHouse) write metrics.
- Mitigations:
  1. Temporarily increase consumer instance count (up to +50%) and rebalance.
  2. If storage write throttle is the cause, apply backpressure at ingest and file a capacity increase request.

3) Runbook: dashboards-api outage (partial or full)
- Symptoms: dashboard panels return 500s or high render latency.
- Immediate checks:
  1. Check dash-api pod health and recent deploys.
  2. Validate Elasticsearch/ClickHouse query latencies.
- Mitigation:
  1. Restart dash-api pods (rolling restart).
  2. If caused by expensive queries, enable fallback summary cache: `curl -XPOST https://dash-api/_cache/fallback` (requires platform-admin token).

Incident retrospectives (Q4 2025 highlights) - summary + actions:
- Incident A: Metrics pipeline backlog (Nov 2025) - root cause: unexpected cardinality increase from a customer integration.
  - Impact: delayed dashboards and missing SLO metrics for 4 hours.
  - Actions: implement hard cardinality guards in metrics-ingest (done), add a rate limit per producer (in progress), and create an automated alert for per-tenant ingestion anomaly (done).

- Incident B: Control-plane partial outage (Dec 2025) - root cause: faulty rollout of routing changes combined with insufficient canary traffic.
  - Impact: API error rate spike ~30 minutes.
  0  - Actions: require mandatory canary success threshold (P95 latency and 0.5% error delta) before full rollout, update CI/CD rollout step to include synthetic smoke tests (ETA: 2026-02-15), and add a rollback automation if canary fails (in progress).

Retrospective action tracker (accepted items):
- Implement per-tenant ingest quotas and anomaly alerts (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-31).
- CI/CD canary gating: add synthetic smoke tests and automatic rollback (owner: eng-infra, due: 2026-02-15).
- Dashboard query cache TTL tuning and support for summary-mode (owner: eng-platform, due: 2026-03-15).

Roadmap (Q2-Q3 2026 prioritized initiatives):
- Q2 2026 (High priority):
  - Automated SLO burn alerting + SLO weekly digest (owner: reliability, deliverable: SLO dashboard & weekly email).
  - Per-tenant ingestion quotas and adaptive rate limiting (owner: observability).
  - CI/CD canary gating + rollback automation (owner: eng-infra).

- Q3 2026 (Medium priority):
  - Declarative alerting rules with test harness (owner: eng-platform) - goal: reduce false positives by 40%.
  - Dashboard performance improvements: move heavy queries into pre-aggregated store (owner: eng-platform + storage).
  - Runbook authoring automation: convert incident transcripts into runbook drafts using the incident-harness tool (owner: platform-ops).

How-to: common operational tasks (short commands and steps)
- Forced rollback for a service (CI/CD Orchestrator):
  1. Find last successful deployment: `ci-cd-cli list-deployments --service platform-controller --limit 5`
  2. Trigger rollback: `ci-cd-cli rollback --service platform-controller --to-deployment <deployment-id> --reason \"incident rollback\"`
  3. Monitor: observe platform-overview and control-plane latency for 10 minutes.

- Add a new dashboard panel (checklist):
  1. Propose panel in #dashboards with query and visualization spec.
  2. Create panel as draft under dash-id: team-temp, include description and owner.
  3. After 24h validation, move to platform-overview if broadly useful.

On-call process and escalation matrix:
- SEV classification: P1 (service down/customer impact), P2 (degraded but functional), P3 (minor issue).
- PagerDuty flows: P1 -> immediate PD paging, 5-minute ack SLA -> escalates if >5m. P2 -> Slack + PD to primary but 30m ack SLA.
- Post-incident: the incident lead must file an incident ticket, schedule a blameless retro within 7 days, and assign owners for action items.

Knowledge base and team wiki pointers:
- Canonical runbooks directory: eng-platform/runbooks (link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks).
- Dashboard library: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards (includes JSON export templates).
- Oncall rota and escalation matrix: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall.
- SLO definitions and SLO dashboard: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-definitions.

Document maintenance and ownership:
- This document owner: eng-platform (document steward: Aisha Patel). Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1 incident.
- Checklist for updates: after each major deploy or runbook change, increment the doc version and add a short changelog entry under the Confluence page.

Appendix: useful commands and quick links
- Inspect pods by label: `kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-controller -o wide`
- Restart a deployment: `kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/platform-controller`
- Query consumer lag (Kafka): `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group metrics-ingest`
- Dashboards: Grafana URL: https://grafana.internal.redwood/, Dash IDs: platform-overview-main, obs-pipeline, cicd-orch.

If you discover missing runbooks or dashboards referenced here, open a GitHub issue in the eng-platform docs repo and assign to the document owner.
